title: Come, Mortals, Come Behold
description: Come, Mortals, Come Behold in Tonic Solfa to QUAM DILECTA, doh is F: the solfa with the words, staff notation, 4 verses and a piano.
about: John Brownlie translated these words from the Greek service books for Hymns from the Greek Office Books (Paisley, 1904), headed “Antiphon”.
The book printed the words without tunes. They are in Sixes (6.6.6.6), and this page sets them to QUAM DILECTA; any other Sixes tune fits them as well.
underlay: Come, mor-tals, come be-hold! He hangs up-on the tree, Who made the roll-ing sea The new formed earth up-hold.

lines: See! He is crowned with thorns,
With clouds that float on air.
With nails His hands are torn,

source: John Brownlie, Hymns from the Greek Office Books (1904)
licence: Public domain: John Brownlie died in 1925.
credits: Translated by John Brownlie (1857–1925) from the Greek, public domain, as printed in Hymns from the Greek Office Books; set to QUAM DILECTA by NoteFusion, as words-only hymn books were sung.
